introduction: On this second Sunday of Lent, God calls Abram to leave his country and go to a land he will show him, promising to bless him. In the Gospel, Jesus is transfigured on the mountain before Peter, James and John, and the Father says, This is my beloved Son; listen to him. Paul tells Timothy that God has called us to a holy life. Let us listen to Jesus and follow where he leads.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord's eye is on those who hope in his love. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may listen to the beloved Son and follow him faithfully. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are called to leave their homes, migrants and missionaries: that God may bless and protect them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are afraid: that Jesus may touch them and say, Rise, and do not be afraid. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who suffer for the Gospel: that God may give them strength. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may set out with faith wherever the Lord calls us. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, you called Abram to set out in faith and you revealed the glory of your Son. Help us to listen to Jesus and to follow him without fear. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Rise, and do not be afraid
reflection.body:
God's call to Abram is short and demanding: "Leave your country, and your relatives, and your father's house, and go to the land that I will show you." Abram is not told where he is going. He is given only a promise: "I will make of you a great nation. I will bless you." And the blessing is not for him alone: "All the families of the earth will be blessed through you." Matthew records his response simply: "So Abram went, as the LORD had told him." Faith begins by setting out.

In the Gospel, Jesus takes Peter, James and John up a high mountain, and "He was changed before them. His face shone like the sun, and his garments became as white as the light." Moses and Elijah appear, talking with him. Peter wants to make the moment last: "Lord, it is good for us to be here."

Then a bright cloud covers them, and a voice says, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him." The disciples fall on their faces, terrified. Then Matthew gives a tender detail: "Jesus came and touched them and said," Get up, and do not be afraid. When they look up, "they saw no one, except Jesus alone."

The Transfiguration gave the disciples a glimpse of Jesus' glory before they faced his Passion. In Lent, we too need to see where the road leads: through the cross to glory.

Paul tells Timothy to bear hardship for the Gospel, relying on God "who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace." Our call, like Abram's, is a gift.

This week, listen to Jesus in the Gospel each day. And if fear holds you back from where God is calling, let him touch you and say: rise, and do not be afraid.
